criterion_scores.reasoning: Nine of the ten numbered spec decisions are encoded correctly and I verified each against both the artifact text and, where a source of truth exists, against me-model.md and target-companies.md (comp rules, dedup re-keying, close-out count, quota-capped SQL, Dice/RSS.app removal all check out precisely, including matching worked-example arithmetic against me-model.md's own worked examples). But decision 1 ('no technical roles') has a real, traceable hole: 'Technical Account Manager' is named as an ideal IC title at line 149 and is not caught by the drop-list, so the pipeline as specified would not actually exclude it despite Alex's explicit ruling and despite the same file having scrubbed Solutions Engineer/Consultant/Sales Engineer everywhere else. That is a behavior-level contradiction of a numbered spec decision, capping this criterion per the rubric's spec-drift rule (≤0.70); I scored below the cap ceiling because the same commit that was supposed to purge this category specifically missed this line, and the file's own git history shows it was never revisited.

All ten spec decisions have corresponding sections, the Roles DB schema is fully specified, Steps 0-6 are all present with no TODO stubs, and every referenced file exists (verified). The gap is the incomplete propagation of the 2026-09-24 'no technical roles' edit into the adjacent v2.2 IC-list (line 149), and a thin Failure-modes section that names only Apollo/schema-drift and not ATS-board network failures, which the primary (and only mandatory) source relies on entirely.

Frontmatter, naming (no alex: prefix, correct for a project skill), MCP/tool naming, and the Notion quota-cap convention are all followed correctly, and cross-checked collection IDs (Companies, People) match the canonical CLAUDE.md list exactly. However the file explicitly claims to 'mirror me-model.md §1.5 (keep in sync)' and I found one concrete divergence: me-model.md's own IC-ideal title list does not include 'Technical Account Manager', so the two files are out of sync on the exact axis this line is supposed to track — a source-of-truth discipline miss, not just a cosmetic slip.

The artifact is otherwise lean and decision-grounded — no duplicated state, no hardcoded secrets, no fabricated numbers (I traced every dollar figure), no resurrected tombstoned tooling (Dice/RSS.app removal is correctly reflected, not resurrected), and speculative surface is generally justified by named rulings. But the Technical Account Manager line is a concrete instance of the exact anti-pattern this criterion names: a previously-excluded category (technical roles, explicitly ruled OUT 2026-09-24) is left standing, unguarded, in a still-live scoring path elsewhere in the same document.

Failure modes and honest-gaps sections exist and are not overclaiming (the LinkedIn-coverage gap is named plainly, not glossed over; the file is transparent about Greenhouse's UNKNOWN-freshness limitation throughout). Comments and warnings (⚠️ callouts) clearly explain intent behind non-obvious rules (Greenhouse updated_at, drop-list-wins, slug traps referenced via target-companies.md). I did not find any docstring/claim asserting a stronger property than the code delivers on the diagnostics axis specifically — the Technical Account Manager gap is a silent one, but it isn't accompanied by an overclaiming statement (nothing in the file claims 'all technical titles are excluded'), so I did not apply the confidence-honesty cap here; scored at the mid anchor for the minor honest-gaps thinness noted in the defects.

defects.quote: Account Manager, Customer Success Manager, Engagement Manager, Technical Account Manager, Account Director, an IC Sales Director.
defects.issue: The Rubric v2.2 IC-vs-people-management example list names 'Technical Account Manager' as an ideal IC title, and the drop-list (line 64: `Engineer|Developer|Designer|Scientist|Researcher|Recruiter|Accountant|Controller|Counsel|Marketing Manager|Product Manager|Program Manager|Content|Brand|Demand Gen`) contains no term that matches 'Technical' — so a real Technical Account Manager posting would pass the keep-list (contains 'Account Manager'), survive the drop-list untouched, and then be actively scored as an ideal-IC title per this line. This is not just a stale example; it is a live functional gap that lets a technical-flavored title back into scoring, directly against decision 1 and the verbatim ruling quoted two lines above the drop-list note ('make sure we are not going technical with any roles'). The 2026-09-24 commit (b18201e) that purged Solutions Engineer/Consultant/Sales Engineer from the keep-list, the drop-list carve-out, and the scoring table did not touch this adjacent line, and it has never been touched since (confirmed via `git log -p --follow` on this file).
defects.decision: (1) FIVE role shapes only; no technical roles (Solutions Engineer/Consultant, Sales Engineer are OUT).

defects.quote: Engagement Manager, Technical Account Manager, Account Director, an IC Sales Director
defects.issue: Naming a technical-flavored title ('Technical Account Manager') as an ideal-IC example, with no drop-list term that excludes it, effectively re-admits the exact category of role ('technical roles') that Alex explicitly ruled OUT on 2026-09-24 and that was deliberately purged elsewhere in this same file (keep-list, drop-list carve-out, scoring table). This is the anti-pattern the rubric names directly: resurrecting an excluded decision in one corner of the artifact while the rest of the file correctly enforces it.
defects.decision: (1) FIVE role shapes only; no technical roles (Solutions Engineer/Consultant, Sales Engineer are OUT).

defects.quote: Mirrors `me-model.md` §1.5 (keep in sync). **Score by the role's *mechanism* (JD language), not its title.**
defects.issue: SKILL.md claims to mirror `me-model.md` §1.5 and stay in sync with it, but `me-model.md`'s own IC-ideal title list (§1.5, 'IC vs. people-management') reads 'Account Manager / Customer Success Manager / Engagement Manager / Account Director / IC Sales Director' — it does NOT include 'Technical Account Manager'. SKILL.md line 149 added that title and the two files have drifted, breaking the source-of-truth discipline this file itself asserts (verified by reading `.claude/references/me-model.md` §1.5 directly).

defects.quote: - **Apollo org not found / API blocked** — Apollo may be blocked on the free plan; if the call fails, report honestly and run on the ATS boards alone. Never fabricate roles.
defects.issue: The Failure modes section covers only Apollo-blocked and Roles-DB schema drift. It does not name the more common failure path for the primary source — an ATS board curl erroring, timing out, or rate-limiting (Greenhouse/Ashby/Lever/Workable) — even though Step 1a fans this out across 31 companies per run. The Step 4 'N companies returned 0 rows' gap-reporting language partially covers this but the dedicated Failure modes section should name it explicitly as its own case, the way it does for Apollo.

defects.quote: - **Gap (high confidence):** this does not see the full LinkedIn Jobs index (API closed, no scraping). RSS.app of saved searches was the intended partial bridge and was removed 2026-09-27 unused; TheirStack (paid) is the option if coverage ever becomes the constraint. Name the gap; don't imply full LinkedIn coverage.
defects.issue: The honest-gaps section names only the LinkedIn-coverage gap. It does not name the Ashby `loc:.location` field's null-safety (Step 1a's Ashby jq projection, unlike Workable's `(.city // "") + ...` pattern, has no fallback for a missing/null location field), which could silently write an empty or malformed Location value and understate location/culture scoring without any error being surfaced.
